alignments.note: The ASV writes the same day with no preposition, so nothing is spent on בְּ (rule 40).
Construct noun with a supplied the and same, no article morpheme present (rules 29, 15); head on the lexeme.
The verbal noun זֶבַח is recast as the finite offer; its own lexeme is what the English verb carries.

No object morpheme stands in the clause, so the supplied object pronoun it answers to nothing and is added under rule 44, which forbids joining such a pronoun to a rendering merely because it stands beside it. Keeping it inside זֶבַח's unit on the ground that the noun names the thing offered was the competing reading, but זֶבַח here names the act, not the victim.
Suffix takes the subject pronoun of the recast clause (rule 18).
Niphal takes dummy subject, auxiliaries and lexical verb (rule 17).
Waw takes and.
מִן rendered by on here; the ASV's word for the morpheme is what is aligned (rule 11).
Supplied the joins the noun (rule 15).
Coordinator and subordinator written contiguously at the clause's left edge are one rendering of the waw (rule 55); headed on the coordinator. Heading on if was the competing reading.
Substantival article takes the supplied pronoun aught and heads on it (rule 41).
Participle takes remain.
Preposition takes until.
Noun takes day.
The only article morpheme in the phrase takes the written the (rule 15).
Ordinal takes third.
Preposition takes with.
Assimilated article token; the ASV writes no the before fire (rules 12, 29).
Noun takes fire.
Niphal takes subject pronoun, auxiliaries and lexical verb.

review_notes: Corrected: the it of ye offer it is now its own added unit. The Hebrew writes no object morpheme in that clause, and rule 44 states that a supplied object pronoun does not join a rendering merely because it stands inside or beside it.
and if is read as one rendering of the waw under rule 55's contiguity test; the two English words are adjacent, so nothing here is a surplus subordinator.
